contributorNote: Turkana (Ng'aturkana) vocabulary compiled from Lieut. Ludwig von Höhnel (1894 "Discovery of Lakes Rudolf and Stefanie"), Sir Harry H. Johnston (1902), Rev. J. B. Purvis (1909 "Through Uganda to Mount Elgon", Ch. XIII), Hon. K. R. Dundas (1910 "Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District", JRAI Vol. 40, pp. 66–70, Plates XVI–XVII — audited 100% line-by-line across 16 principal tribes, 19 Ngoitunya/Ngolio attegir clans, 6 life stages, asavanissia ages, Nessegonn bush, marriage & slaughter customs, Agipie & nether-world god, and 12-month Nakiborror/Nakamou/Nait calendar), Mervyn W. H. Beech (1911), and Juxon Barton (1921). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (Sunbird AI SALT & SALT-31 Ng'aturkana (CC-BY-4.0), CLDF ASJP v20 TURKANA (Best 1983 / Brown, CC-BY-4.0), SIL Bloom Ng'aturkana CC-BY-4.0).

entries.english: Ngaruwo (The Rain-Makers' Clan of the Turkana) in Dundas (1910, p. 67)
entries.translation: Ngaruwo (12th clan of the Ngoitunya and Ngolio tribes)
entries.context: Hon. K. R. Dundas, Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District, JRAI Vol. 40 (1910, p. 67) • Cross-verified with Sunbird AI SALT & SALT-31 Ng'aturkana (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Male Life-Stage Terms (Nidue, Egile, Kasikou & Oppa) & Asavanissia Warrior Age-Generations in Dundas (1910, p. 67)
entries.translation: nidue (young boy) → egile (warrior) → kasikou / oppa (old man; oppa wears a beaded cap-like headdress, Plate XVI Fig. 7) • asavanissia (warrior age-generations instituted every 4 or 5 years)
entries.context: Hon. K. R. Dundas, Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District, JRAI Vol. 40 (1910, p. 67 & Plate XVI Fig. 7) • Cross-verified with Sunbird AI SALT & SALT-31 Ng'aturkana (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Female Life-Stage Terms (Apesur, Aberu & Agemat) in Dundas (1910, p. 67)
entries.translation: apesur (unmarried girl; wears V-shaped bead-and-ostrich-eggshell apron in front and wide hide skirt behind, Plate XVI Fig. 2) → aberu (married woman / wife; wears gazelle or goat-skin apron) → agemat (old woman)
entries.context: Hon. K. R. Dundas, Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District, JRAI Vol. 40 (1910, p. 67 & Plate XVI Fig. 2) • Cross-verified with Sunbird AI SALT & SALT-31 Ng'aturkana (CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Agipie (Benevolent Sky God) & the Malevolent Nether-World God of Rocks and Rivers in Dundas (1910, p. 69)
entries.translation: Agipie (benevolent god of the skies, prayed to with an ox, sheep, or goat sacrifice in sickness) vs. the malevolent god dwelling in the nether world, rocks, and rivers (a thunderstorm is the two gods fighting and hurling lightning at each other)
entries.context: Hon. K. R. Dundas, Notes on the Tribes Inhabiting the Baringo District, JRAI Vol. 40 (1910, p. 69) • Cross-verified with Sunbird AI SALT & SALT-31 Ng'aturkana (CC-BY-4.0)
